Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios and adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
sections.results: After adjustment for confounders, quadrivalent human papillomavirus vaccination was associated with lower odds of all included adverse pregnancy outcomes. Statistically significant associations were observed for preterm birth (<37 weeks) (adjusted odds ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.91 to 0.99), very preterm birth (28 weeks to 31 weeks) (0.85, 0.75 to 0.97), spontaneous preterm birth (0.95, 0.91 to 0.99), preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (0.93, 0.87 to 1.00), and severe small for gestational age infant (0.92, 0.87 to 0.97). Risk reduction was generally more pronounced among women vaccinated at younger ages.
sections.conclusion: Quadrivalent human papillomavirus vaccination before pregnancy was associated with a lower risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, particularly among women vaccinated at earlier ages, extending benefits of human papillomavirus vaccination beyond cancer prevention.

items.title: Deep learning-based prediction of one-year functional and structural outcomes in treatment-naïve DMO after anti-VEGF therapy.

sections.objective: To evaluate whether baseline structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans contain prognostic information that can be used by deep learning models to predict one-year functional and anatomical outcomes in treatment-naïve diabetic macular oedema (DMO).
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study. Eighty-seven eyes (74 patients) with treatment-naïve DMO receiving intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy. Baseline OCT volumes were analysed using a deep learning regression model. The images were homogenised - preprocessed and transformed into a common reference frame - to streamline the learning task. The model predicted 12-month changes in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and central subfield thickness (CST). Performance was assessed using 5-fold cross-validation and compared between original and preprocessed datasets. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated classification of responders versus non-responders, while occlusion sensitivity analysis identified image regions contributing most to predictions.
sections.results: Mean BCVA improved from 0.40 ± 0.40 to 0.33 ± 0.30 logMAR, and CST decreased from 390.2 ± 77.1 µm to 342.2 ± 76.3 µm (both p < 0.001). Prediction of BCVA change achieved an R² of 0.575, improving to 0.661 after preprocessing. CST prediction improved from R² = 0.447-0.633. Classification performance increased from AUC 0.65 to 0.71 for BCVA response and from 0.93 to 0.97 for CST response. Key predictive regions included the outer retina and retinal pigment epithelium.
sections.conclusion: Deep learning analysis of baseline OCT can predict one-year outcomes in DMO. Image homogenisation enhances performance, and responder identification suggests the potential utility of this approach for prognostic assessment and risk stratification, warranting further validation before clinical implementation.

items.title: Retinal nerve fibre layer thickness change in the parapapillary region.

sections.objective: To assess radial changes in the retinal nerve fibre layer thickness (RNFLT) in the temporal parapapillary region.
sections.methods: Using radial optical coherence tomographic images of the optic nerve head, we measured in a sample of participants of the population-based Beijing Eye Study the RNFLT in the temporal horizontal parapapillary region at locations 'A' (intact inner (INL) and outer (ONL) nuclear layer), 'B' (INL/ONL end), 'C' (just beyond the INL/ONL end) in the parapapillary gamma zone centre and at the disc border. Exclusion criterion was any optic nerve damage including glaucoma.
sections.results: The study included 47 eyes (47 participants). RNFLT increased (p<0.001) from 86±24 µm at 'A' (optic disc centre distance (ODCD): 1523±477 µm) to 128±42 µm at 'B' (ODCD: 1192±394 µm) and to 190±64 µm at 'C' (ODCD: 1023±312 µm). The increasing RNFLT measurements from location 'A' to 'B' by 49% and from 'B' to 'C' by 49% were double as high as geometrically expected ('A' to 'B': 1523 µm/1192 µm (28%); 'B' to 'C': 1192 µm/1023 µm (17%)). In the temporal parapapillary gamma zone (detected in 23 eyes), RNFLT changed from the mid of gamma zone (ODCD: 1069±291 µm) to the disc border (ODCD: 618±228 µm) from 210±76 µm to 238±81 µm (or +13%), while the ODCD decreased by 42%.
sections.conclusion: RNFLT in the temporal horizontal parapapillary region markedly increased just beyond (in direction to the disc border) of the INL/ONL end while within gamma zone RNFLT changed only marginally. Absence of underlying INL/ONL was associated with pronounced RNFL thickening, without major further radial RNFLT changes in gamma zone. These findings may be of importance for RNFLT measurements in highly myopic eyes.

items.title: Association between varicose veins and central serous chorioretinopathy.

sections.methods: Propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients with varicose veins (n=621 513) were matched 1:1 to controls without varicose veins on age, sex, race and ethnicity, with prior CSCR or serous pigment epithelial detachment (PED) excluded. A secondary analysis excluded glucocorticoid users and additionally matched on hypertension, sleep apnoea and healthcare utilisation. A tertiary analysis compared thromboembolic risk (pulmonary embolism (PE) and deep vein thrombosis (DVT)) in varicose vein patients with and without CSCR.
sections.results: Varicose veins were significantly associated with CSCR (risk ratio (RR) 2.16; 95% CI 1.86 to 2.52; p<0.0001) and serous PED (RR 1.97; 95% CI 1.69 to 2.93; p<0.0001). Associations persisted after excluding glucocorticoid users and adjusting for comorbidities (CSCR RR 1.83; 95% CI 1.22 to 2.75; p=0.003; PED RR 1.95; 95% CI 1.38 to 3.34; p=0.013). Among varicose vein patients, rates of DVT (RR 1.36; p=0.078) and PE (RR 1.41; p=0.14) did not differ significantly between those with and without CSCR.
sections.conclusion: Varicose veins were significantly associated with CSCR and serous PED, independent of glucocorticoid exposure and known comorbidities, supporting a possible systemic vascular mechanism in CSCR pathophysiology.
sections.other: AimTo investigate the association between varicose veins and central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR), based on emerging genetic evidence of a shared vascular mechanism.

items.title: Twelve-Month Results of Cyanoacrylate Closure in Patients with Venous Leg Ulceration.

sections.objective: Venous leg ulceration (VLU) is a major cause of patient distress and healthcare burden. Previous studies have highlighted the importance of early endovenous ablation of superficial venous reflux to expedite healing and prevent recurrence, but the optimal venous ablation modality is unclear. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of cyanoacrylate closure in patients with VLU.
sections.methods: A global, prospective, single-arm observational study was conducted in 17 centers across the United States and Europe. A total of 125 participants with VLU were included and treated with the VenaSeal closure system, in addition to standard wound therapy, including multilayered compression. Adjuvant treatments to varicosities, perforators or the sub-ulcer plexus were left to the discretion of treating clinicians. The primary outcome was VLU healing through 12 months. Secondary outcomes included time to ulcer recurrence, anatomic vein closure, target limb adverse events, and changes in quality-of-life measures.
sections.results: One hundred twenty-five participants with VLU and saphenous vein reflux were enrolled. The mean (± standard deviation) age was 67.9 ± 14.76 years, with 38.4% females and an overall mean BMI of 32.4± 9.35. Concomitant foam sclerotherapy treatments were performed in 19.7% (31/157) of target veins. At 12 months, ulcer healing was 81.3% and ulcer recurrence was 17.0%. The median time to ulcer healing was 92 days (95% CI 74, 137). Anatomic vein closure was successful in 82.7% of all target veins. CEC-adjudicated AE and SAEs included: 2 granulomas, 1 hypersensitivity reaction, and 4 cases of phlebitis of the treated limb. Healthcare services utilized outside of the index procedure yielded 0.12 adjunctive therapies per vein-year. Venous-specific and generic QoL scores showed sustained improvement compared to baseline scores.
sections.conclusion: VenaSeal effectively eliminated saphenous reflux in patients with VLU. The ulcer healing rate was high, and the recurrence rate was low. Complication rates were also low and QoL improved.

items.title: Mitomycin C Application during Trabeculectomy-Injection versus Sponge: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

sections.objective: To evaluate the recently published literature on the efficacy and safety outcomes of delivering mitomycin C (MMC) by either sub-Tenon's/subconjunctival injection (MMC-I) or by sponge (MMC-S) during trabeculectomy surgery.
sections.methods: A literature search was last conducted in the PubMed database in May 2026 and yielded 135 articles. Eighteen full-text articles were reviewed, and 11 met all inclusion criteria for this assessment and were assigned a level of evidence rating by the panel methodologist.
sections.results: Six studies were rated level I, 2 were rated level II, and 3 were rated level III. The racial and ethnic backgrounds of study participants represented a diverse mix, and in many studies, a variety of glaucoma diagnoses were included, the majority of which were primary open-angle glaucoma. The MMC-I technique was reported to have used a wider range of drug concentrations (0.05-0.4 mg/mL) than MMC-S (0.1-0.4 mg/mL). The complete success rate of intraocular pressure (IOP) control ranged from 40.3% to 90.9% in the MMC-I group compared with 17.7% to 86.5% in the MMC-S group. The wide range of success rates may be a result of differences in definitions of success, follow-up time, and patient populations. Change in IOP from baseline ranged from 2.8 mmHg (17%) to 19.4 mmHg (58%) in the MMC-I group compared with 5.8 mmHg (31%) to 18.0 mmHg (59%) in the MMC-S group. No significant differences in complications, such as rates of bleb leak, hypotony, choroidal effusion, or choroidal hemorrhage, were reported. Two studies reported significantly fewer 5-fluorouracil injections in the MMC-I group, and 1 reported more glaucoma surgery reoperations in the MMC-S group. Several studies reported a more favorable bleb morphology that was diffuse, lower profile, and less vascular in the MMC-I group than in the MMC-S group.
sections.conclusion: Although MMC-I may offer some advantages over MMC-S trabeculectomy with respect to bleb morphology, level I and II evidence supports the application of MMC using either injection or sponges during trabeculectomy. Both applications result in similar rates of surgical success (a lower IOP and a reduction in medication burden) and have a similar safety profile.

items.title: Symptomatic popliteal artery entrapment syndrome: a challenging diagnosis and treatment.

sections.objective: We analysed the diagnostic accuracy, patient selection, and postoperative outcomes of patients surgically treated for popliteal artery entrapment syndrome (PAES).
sections.methods: All patients diagnosed with PAES in our hospital between January 2019 and March 2025 were included. Diagnosis was made on the positive triad of symptoms, decreased ankle-brachial index (ABI) and compression on angiography. Conservative and operative treatments were offered to all patients. Retrospective analysis of demographic, clinical, and surgical data was performed.
sections.results: Thirty-two patients were diagnosed with PAES with a total of 57 affected legs. Thirty-five legs in 21 patients underwent surgical decompression. Functional success was achieved in 60.0% and technical success in 85.7% of the operated legs. Positive evolution in the ABI is seen with prolonged follow up. Fourteen legs experienced no functional improvement after surgery, despite evidence of technical success in nine legs (25.7%). Five patients were postoperatively diagnosed with other causal pathologies than PAES and two patients experienced symptom relieve with botulinum toxin infiltration postoperatively.
sections.conclusion: PAES is a pathology with a broad differential diagnosis. The difference between postoperative functional and technical success in patients with popliteal artery compression indicates that other pathologies may be responsible for the patient's symptoms and that the popliteal compression may be an asymptomatic coincidence. PAES should be considered a diagnosis of exclusion in a multidisciplinary setting when the positive triad is present, to maximize the postoperative functional success. To determine technical success, prolonged ABI follow-up is recommended, as improvement may occur over time.

items.title: Hashimoto's thyroiditis: two decades on.
items.abstract: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is the most common cause of primary hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient regions and is characterised by immune-mediated injury to thyroid follicular cells. Its pathophysiology involves an interplay of genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and epigenetic modifications that disrupt immune tolerance, promoting T-cell mediated thyroid injury and thyroid autoantibody production. The disease can progress from euthyroid autoimmunity to subclinical and overt hypothyroidism, with substantial variation in its course. Clinical manifestations vary with the extent of thyroid dysfunction and inflammatory activity. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, thyroid function testing, thyroid autoantibody measurement, and ultrasonography when indicated. Management centres on levothyroxine replacement for overt hypothyroidism, with an individualised approach to subclinical disease. Thyroidectomy is reserved for selected indications, whereas emerging immunomodulatory strategies remain investigational. This Review synthesises developments over the past two decades in the epidemiology, natural history, aetiopathogenesis, diagnosis, and management of Hashimoto's thyroiditis, and considers emerging mechanistic insights and approaches to precision medicine that might inform future disease-modifying therapies.

items.title: Incidence of clinically diagnosed infections in children with sickle cell anaemia treated with oral hydroxyurea in Angola, DR Congo, Kenya, and Uganda: a retrospective cohort study from the REACH trial.

sections.objective: Hydroxyurea is widely used in the first-line treatment of sickle cell anaemia; however, its mildly myelosuppressive effects when used at therapeutic doses have led to suggestions that treatment with hydroxyurea might increase the risk of infection. To address this question, we have investigated the incidence of clinically diagnosed infections among children within the Realizing Effectiveness Across Continents with Hydroxyurea (REACH) trial during various phases of hydroxyurea treatment.
sections.methods: REACH (NCT01966731 and NCT06171217) is an ongoing, phase 1/2, open-label, multicentre treatment trial of children with sickle cell anaemia with 2 months of screening followed by oral hydroxyurea at a fixed dose for 6 months and then dose escalation to the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). The current international, retrospective cohort study included children aged 1-10 years with sickle cell anaemia who were recruited and enrolled into REACH from four hospitals in Angola, DR Congo, Kenya, and Uganda and who had previously been followed up within the trial. Clinically diagnosed infections were characterised by likely aetiology and severity and incidence rate ratios (IRR) were then computed across time and during dosing phases as protocol-specified outcomes. The primary outcome of the current analysis was the incidence of clinically diagnosed infections, which was stratified by hydroxyurea treatment phase and assessed in all children who started fixed-dose hydroxyurea treatment. Rates of each clinically diagnosed infection (per 100 person-years of observation [PYO]) were calculated by age group and dosing phase.
sections.results: Between July 4, 2014, and Nov 11, 2016, 635 children were enrolled in the trial. 606 children (296 [49%] female and 310 [51%] male) completed screening and began treatment with hydroxyurea. Overall, 5493 infections occurred across 5638 PYO, with an incidence rate of 97·4/100 PYO. Among non-malarial infections, rates declined from the screening to fixed-dose phase (adjusted IRR 0·81 [95% CI 0·67-0·98]) and decreased further from the screening to the MTD phase (0·51 [0·43-0·61]; p<0·0001). Statistically significant decreases across the fixed-dose, dose-escalation, and MTD phases, respectively, were observed in the adjusted IRRs for upper respiratory tract infections (IRR 0·84 [95% CI 0·62-1·14], 0·77 [0·58-1·03], and 0·64 [0·47-0·88]; p=0·0051), lower respiratory tract infections (1·26 [0·69-2·31], 0·60 [0·32-1·12], and 0·45 [0·23-0·89]; p=0·021), bacterial skin or nail infections (0·58 [0·26-1·30], 0·32 [0·15-0·68], and 0·31 [0·14-0·66]; p=0·0025), and non-specific infectious syndromes (0·80 [0·58-1·11], 0·47 [0·35-0·63], and 0·39 [0·28-0·53]; p<0·0001). A similar decrease was observed for the adjusted IRR of grade 3 or higher infections across the fixed-dose, dose-escalation, and MTD phases, respectively (0·65 [0·42-1·00], 0·20 [0·13-0·32], and 0·48 [0·32-0·73]; p=0·0006).
sections.conclusion: In the large REACH cohort, the incidence rate or severity of clinically diagnosed infections in children with sickle cell anaemia living in sub-Saharan Africa, was not increased during the hydroxyurea treatment phases of this trial. Our results provide reassurance that, even when administered at MTD, hydroxyurea does not put children with sickle cell anaemia at increased risk of illness or death from infections. For the French, Portuguese and Swahili translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Epidemiological trends of HIV among individuals aged 15-54 years in South Africa from 2004 to 2025: a population-based, longitudinal cohort study.

sections.objective: South Africa has mounted the largest HIV prevention and treatment programme in history, delivering substantial gains in survival and prevention of new HIV infections; however, service disruptions and recent funding losses might jeopardise these successes. There is a scarcity of high-quality, population-based empirical evidence on key epidemic metrics needed to accurately gauge recent progress towards epidemic control in South Africa. We aimed to evaluate recent progress towards HIV epidemic control in South Africa by quantifying long-term trends in key epidemic control metrics in a large population-based cohort in rural KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
sections.methods: In this population-based, longitudinal cohort study, we used prospectively collected HIV testing, sociodemographic, behavioural, and population viral load data from the Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) health and demographic surveillance system in rural KwaZulu-Natal from 2003 to 2025. Population-based HIV surveys (encompassing individual health interview and HIV testing) take place annually in all consenting resident individuals aged 15 years or older. We used Poisson regression models to quantify trends in directly observed HIV incidence in repeat testers (aged 15-54 years) who had initially tested negative for HIV and subsequently received at least one valid HIV test result. We further analysed 11 rounds of population viral load testing conducted between 2011 and 2025. We used generalised estimating equations to quantify population viral suppression metrics and calculated trends in the incidence-to-prevalence ratio, a key metric for evaluating progress towards epidemic control.
sections.results: Between June 24, 2003, and May 22, 2025, across the population cohort, 59 806 (65·4%) of 91 367 contacted individuals aged 15-54 years consented to participate at least once in population-based HIV testing. Of those tested, 33 754 (56·4%) were female and 26 052 (43·6%) were male, with a median age of 26·7 years (IQR 19·3-39·1) at testing date. Among 42 662 participants who initially tested HIV negative and were recontacted, 29 702 (69·6%) underwent repeat HIV testing and were included in the incidence analysis. In this group, over 182 112 person-years of observation, we observed 4852 HIV seroconversions. From 2013 to 2018, overall annual HIV incidence rates declined by 52·2% in males and 36·9% in females. We found no evidence of a continued downward trend in HIV incidence between 2019 and 2025 among either females or males. After a period of substantial decline (from 2011 to 2018), population detectable viraemia increased significantly from 2019 to 2025 by 9·6 percentage points (95% CI 5·4-13·8), remaining an estimated 30·7 percentage points (95% CI 27·2-34·3) below the UNAIDS 95-95-95 population viral suppression target. The incidence-to-prevalence ratio decreased substantially across consecutive survey rounds, from 0·132 (95% CI 0·114-0·152) in 2006 to its lowest recorded value of 0·034 (95% CI 0·028-0·042) in 2022, representing an overall 74·2% decline. After 2022, the ratio stagnated above the epidemic control benchmark of 0·03.
sections.conclusion: These epidemic metrics show that progress towards HIV epidemic control is faltering in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The tools to reverse this trajectory are available; the challenge now is to ensure their sustained and effective implementation through coordinated action across research, policy, government, civil society, and international funding partners. We can, and we should, change course now if we want to achieve an AIDS-free generation in South Africa and the world.

items.title: Management of Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Routine US Clinical Practice: Impact of Delayed Treatment Initiation.

sections.objective: To understand management of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in routine US clinical practice to identify gaps in patient care.
sections.methods: Retrospective analysis of electronic medical records from the Vestrum database. Treatment-naive eyes newly diagnosed with nAMD from January 1, 2014, with ≥1-years' follow-up. Cumulative incidence of eyes receiving treatment was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier, and factors predicting anti-VEGF receipt through 1 year were evaluated by logistic regression. Proportion of eyes treated over 3 years, baseline factors associated with receiving treatment within 1 year of diagnosis and with delayed (3-12 months after diagnosis) versus prompt (within 29 days of diagnosis) treatment initiation.
sections.results: Of 90 681 eyes included in the analysis, 23% did not receive anti-VEGF treatment at diagnosis, declining to 16%, 15%, and 13% at years 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Mean baseline VA of eyes not treated and treated was 39 and 52 letters, respectively. Eyes were more likely to receive treatment (odds ratio [OR] ≥ 1.50, [95% CI]) if they had baseline VA 20/40-20/100 versus ≥ 20/40 (1.52 [1.44, 1.61]), macular edema (3.26 [3.11, 3.42]), subretinal fluid (4.97 [4.75, 5.20]), or subretinal pigment epithelium fluid (1.64 [1.56, 1.72]). Eyes were less likely to receive treatment (OR ≤ 0.50) if they had simultaneous bilateral diagnosis of nAMD vs. unilateral diagnosis (0.32 [0.31, 0.34]), or baseline VA 9 injections, respectively. In eyes that received >9 injections, those with baseline VA < 20/400 gained 27.2 letters.
sections.conclusion: Overall, approximately one-quarter of eyes with nAMD were not treated within 29 days of diagnosis. Simultaneous bilateral nAMD diagnosis and poor baseline VA (< 20/400) were primary factors associated with not receiving anti-VEGF treatment. Greater VA gains were observed with prompt treatment and increasing number of injections.

items.title: Diverse infections transcriptionally reprogram the intestinal epithelium and epithelial-immune cell interactions.
items.abstract: The distal small intestine has a vital role in host physiology through its regulation of nutrient and fluid homeostasis. Despite being affected in Crohn's disease and serving as a major target for a range of infections, we know relatively little about the complexity of cellular responses and cell-cell communication in the ileum during infection. Here we present GutPath, an atlas of over 500,000 single cells with RNA and protein expression profiles for 91 cell states in the ileum across diverse infectious archetypes. We show that GutPath accurately captures established immune responses to infection while revealing pathogen-specific responses in enterocytes. To highlight the discovery potential of this atlas, we identify a new enterocyte transcriptional state present during Yersinia pseudotuberculosis infection that is spatially linked to bacterial load and tissue pathology. GutPath establishes a much-needed resource for the immunology community that will accelerate the study of transcriptional diversity in the cellular landscapes of the small intestine.

items.title: Transient receptor potential channel activation targets multiple stages of the schistosome parasite.
items.abstract: Schistosomiasis, a neglected tropical disease caused by infection with parasitic blood flukes of the genus Schistosoma , affects more than 250 million people worldwide. Currently, patients rely on a single medicine, praziquantel (PZQ), discovered half a century ago. To combat drug resistance and reach elimination of the schistosome parasite, alternative drugs to PZQ are required that treat and prevent disease. Here, we describe a drug candidate, M5493, with potent activity against multiple parasite life cycle stages. The target is a parasite transient receptor potential ion channel, distinct from the target of PZQ. To circumvent its limited bioavailability, the active agent was converted to prodrug M5493, which displayed robust activity against the schistosome parasite at doses as low as 5 milligrams per kilogram in mice infected with Schistosoma mansoni . Unlike the benzodiazepine meclonazepam, which displays clinical antihelminthic activity through the same target, M5493 showed no sedating side effects given that it did not engage GABA A receptors. Overall, this compound has the potential to provide single-dose treatment, broad-spectrum efficacy against schistosome parasites at different life cycle stages, and transmission blocking activity.

items.title: Neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy for unresectable, homologous recombination deficiency-positive, high-grade serous ovarian cancer (NANT): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery is standard treatment for advanced ovarian cancer that is unlikely to achieve optimal cytoreduction. We aimed to evaluate a chemotherapy-free regimen of neoadjuvant niraparib monotherapy in homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive disease initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery.
sections.methods: This single-arm, phase 2 trial was conducted at six tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, had treatment-naïve, FIGO stage III-IV HRD-positive high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian cancer, an ECOG performance status of 0-2, with a low likelihood of complete primary debulking surgery based on prespecified criteria. Patients received oral niraparib monotherapy for two 28-day cycles with an individualised starting dose of 200 mg or 300 mg. Protocol-permitted supportive care was provided as clinically indicated. Co-primary endpoints were investigator-assessed objective response rate in the response-evaluable population and R0 resection rate after interval debulking surgery in the operated population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of niraparib. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04507841), is closed to enrolment, and this report presents the primary analysis.
sections.results: Between Jan 8, 2021, and Jul 18, 2023, 127 patients were screened, and 67 were enrolled into the study. All enrolled patients were female and self-identified as Han Chinese (median age 55 years [IQR 50-62]). At the data cutoff (Dec 29, 2025), median follow-up was 37·7 months (IQR 31·8-48·5). Among 48 response-evaluable patients, 30 achieved an objective response, with an objective response rate of 63% (95% CI 47-76). Among 40 operated patients, 32 achieved R0 resection, with an R0 resection rate of 80% (95% CI 64-91). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were thrombocytopenia in 32 (48%) of 67 patients, leukopenia in 13 (19%) patients, anaemia in 12 (18%) patients, and neutropenia in nine (13%) patients. Serious adverse events occurred in 19 (28%) patients. No treatment-related deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: Neoadjuvant niraparib showed anti-tumour activity and enabled R0 resection in selected patients with HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer who were initially unsuitable for primary debulking surgery. This strategy remains investigational and requires randomised validation against standard platinum-taxane neoadjuvant chemotherapy. For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among high-risk patients in India, 2023-25: a multicentre prospective study.

sections.objective: Melioidosis is not a nationally notifiable disease in India, and the absence of systematic surveillance has contributed to substantial under-recognition and fragmented epidemiological data. We aimed to determine the hospital-based prevalence of culture-confirmed melioidosis among hospitalised adults at high risk of melioidosis in India.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective, multicentre, hospital-based prevalence study between Jan 1, 2023, and Dec 31, 2025, across 15 tertiary care centres in India. Adults (aged ≥18 years) hospitalised with predefined community-acquired infectious syndromes and diabetes or chronic kidney disease were enrolled. Melioidosis was defined by culture confirmation. The primary outcome was hospital-based prevalence. Prespecified secondary analyses assessed geographical, syndrome-specific, and seasonal variation; factors associated with melioidosis; and clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes.
sections.results: Among 2953 patients, 262 (8·9% [95% CI 7·9-10·0]) had culture-confirmed melioidosis, with marked geographical heterogeneity. Prevalence was highest in Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka, and among patients presenting with extrapulmonary abscesses and bone and joint infections. Cases clustered during the monsoon months. Factors independently associated with melioidosis included monsoon admission (adjusted odds ratio 1·40 [95% CI 1·08-1·83]), male sex (2·33 [1·64-3·32]), outdoor high-risk occupation (1·94 [1·47-2·56]), and groundwater as the primary drinking-water source (3·25 [2·48-4·26]). Bacteraemia occurred in 152 (58%) of 262 patients with melioidosis, and 50 (19%) died in hospital.
sections.conclusion: Melioidosis is a frequent and severe infection among high-risk hospitalised adults in India, with substantial geographical variation and strong environmental and seasonal associations. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing and heightened clinical awareness among high-risk patients.

items.title: Evidence of artemisinin partial resistance in Zambia: a molecular epidemiology and clinical study.

sections.objective: Artemisinin derivatives are central to first-line treatment of both uncomplicated and severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Emerging artemisinin partial resistance in east Africa threatens to spread across the continent.
sections.methods: In two cross-sectional studies conducted across the ten provinces of Zambia in 2024, we genotyped the artemisinin resistance-associated gene Pfkelch13. Children aged 6-72 months were recruited from randomly selected households in the first study, and patients 6 months or older presenting with malarial symptoms at 100 selected health facilities were recruited in the second study. In Kaoma, western Zambia, we recruited patients aged 12 months or older with microscopically confirmed P falciparum infection and a positive rapid diagnostic test. We evaluated the association between Pfkelch13 genotype and day 3 parasite positivity following treatment with artemisinin-based combination therapy, as well as ex-vivo parasite susceptibility to dihydroartemisinin (the active metabolite of artemisinin). We also assessed longitudinal changes in Pfkelch13 mutation prevalence in Kaoma using isolates collected during therapeutic efficacy studies and community surveys conducted from 2018 to 2026.
sections.results: We identified a novel mutation, Pfkelch13 A724E, in 113 (52%) of 217 isolates (95% CI 45-59) from Western Province, 94 (51%) of 184 isolates (95% CI 44-59) from North-Western Province, and 229 (11·7%) of 1949 isolates countrywide. In Kaoma, 28% (21 of 75 [95% CI 18-40]) of patients carrying Pfkelch13 A724E mutant parasites before treatment were parasite-positive on day 3, compared with 0% (zero of 23; [0-15]) of patients with the wild-type allele (p=0·0026). Within the patients who were positive at day 3, the proportion of A724E mutant parasites increased significantly after treatment (p=0·0039). The prevalence of Pfkelch13 A724E in Kaoma increased steadily from 0% (0 of 15 isolates [95% CI 0-22]) in 2018 to 79% (132 of 167 [73-85]) in 2026. No significant ex-vivo growth inhibition was observed in Pfkelch13 A724E parasites after dihydroartemisinin exposure.
sections.conclusion: A novel Pfkelch13 mutation clinically associated with partial resistance to artemisinin is spreading in Zambia. Additional clinical evaluations are urgently needed in the region.

items.title: Regional expansion and adaptive evolution of multidrug-resistant Candida tropicalis in China: a retrospective, multicentre, genomic study.

sections.objective: The emergence of antifungal-resistant Candida tropicalis poses a severe threat to human health and complicates clinical management, yet the molecular epidemiology and mechanisms underlying its resistance and persistence in hospital settings remain poorly understood. We aimed to investigate the regional epidemiology, persistence and virulence trade-offs, and adaptive traits associated with the expansion of multidrug-resistant C tropicalis.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective, multicentre, genomic study of C tropicalis isolates from 84 hospitals in east China and included additional multidrug-resistant (resistant to azoles and echinocandins) isolates from active surveillance at Shanghai East Hospital. We analysed clinical metadata from this hospital to identify risk factors for multidrug-resistant isolate recovery and 30-day mortality. We conducted whole-genome sequencing, RNA sequencing, phenotypic assays, and experimental evolution to elucidate resistance mechanisms, virulence dynamics, and adaptive traits.
sections.results: 1184 clinical isolates from Jan 1, 2017, to Dec 31, 2024, were included; of these, 356 (30·1%) were azole resistant and 98 (8·3%) were multidrug resistant. We identified the regional expansion of a multidrug-resistant C tropicalis lineage, DST849, which accounted for 92 (94%) of 98 multidrug-resistant cases and was predominantly isolated from the urinary tract. Admission to a surgical ward (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 46·37, 95% CI 17·48-123·00) and intubation (32·30, 10·28-101·45) were key risk factors for multidrug-resistant isolate recovery. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that multidrug-resistant C tropicalis isolation was an independent predictor of 30-day mortality (aOR 2·84, 95% CI 1·31-6·16; p=0·0081). Phylogenomic analysis revealed that multidrug-resistant isolates evolved from azole-resistant ancestors (DST225) via the acquisition of FKS1 mutations (S30P) while retaining ERG11 mutations (Y132F and S154F) and acquired a distinguishing ICL1 (Y43T) loss-of-heterozygosity mutation.
sections.conclusion: Our findings reveal the emergence of multidrug-resistant Ctropicalis through lineage-specific expansion, driven by genetic plasticity and adaptive stress responses. These adaptations might facilitate persistence under antifungal and environmental pressures in health-care settings. These insights underscore the urgent need for improved antifungal stewardship, targeted genomic surveillance, and interventions to mitigate multidrug-resistant fungal threats.

items.title: A spatiotemporal lifecycle atlas decodes spatial coordination in rice.
items.abstract: How gene expression programs are coordinated across space and time to build a complete plant remains poorly understood. Here, we combine high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and a gap-free reference genome to build a 3D spatiotemporal atlas of rice, spanning 10 organs and 61 stages from seed to seed. Our datasets profile 851,725 nuclei and 347,640 spatial bins, defining 119 cell types and 133 subtypes across the rice lifecycle. Through multimodal integration, we reconstruct an inferred developmental trajectory graph that links cell states from the proembryo to mature organs and identifies trajectory-associated regulators. We further implicate the pleiotropic regulator OsARF1 in distinct spatial gene programs across developmental contexts. We also uncover widespread axis-associated transcriptional asymmetry, including dorsoventral endosperm programs that partition starch and protein accumulation. Collectively, this high-resolution atlas provides a spatiotemporal framework for understanding rice development and guiding future crop improvement.

items.title: Cancer competition for vitamin B2 creates metabolic checkpoint for T cell ferroptosis.
items.abstract: Metabolic competition between tumors and T cells drives immune evasion, but the transporters and mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here, we establish the CareSLCs platform and identify that SLC52A3-mediated vitamin B2 (VB2) uptake is indispensable for T cell antitumor immunity. Mechanistically, VB2 deficiency impairs mitochondrial respiration and glutathione regeneration, leading to mitophagy, labile iron accumulation, and lipid peroxidation that trigger T cell ferroptosis. Unexpectedly, tumors preferentially employ SLC52A2, not SLC52A3, to scavenge VB2 and outcompete T cells. Tumor SLC52A2 ablation enhances T cell function in immunocompetent hosts without appreciably affecting intrinsic tumor growth. Clinically, high tumoral SLC52A2 correlates with T cell dysfunction and poor survival, whereas dietary VB2 intake is associated with reduced cancer risks. Thus, VB2 supplementation or SLC52A3 overexpression augments CAR-T cell antitumor efficacy. Our results suggest that tumoral VB2 competition establishes a metabolic checkpoint driving T cell ferroptosis and that enhancing VB2 uptake reinvigorates T cells to improve cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: SPARCS enables scalable recovery of complex image-based phenotypes for genetic screening.
items.abstract: Forward genetic screening links genotype to phenotype by introducing random genetic perturbations and identifying phenotype-altering mutations. Although genome-scale screens are routine for simple phenotypes in cultured cells, extending them to complex image-based phenotypes remains challenging. Here, we present spatially resolved CRISPR screening (SPARCS), a microscopy-based platform for forward genetic screening on single-cell images. SPARCS physically isolates mutants in situ by automated laser microdissection, enabling image-based screening at unprecedented scale with multimodal hit phenotyping. We demonstrate SPARCS in genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens of autophagosome formation and activation of the immune sensor STING across 70 million cells. Via machine learning-based image analysis, SPARCS recovered most macroautophagy genes and identified GPHR as a pH-dependent regulator of STING. Mass spectrometry-based proteomics of isolated hit cells revealed endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/Golgi disruption and nominated additional STING regulators via in silico perturbation modeling. These results establish SPARCS as a scalable platform for genome-wide genetic screening of complex cellular phenotypes with a proteome-level readout.

items.title: A non-canonical function of glutathione to suppress ferroptosis via FSP1.
items.abstract: It is well established that glutathione (GSH) is mainly utilized by glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) to diminish peroxidized phospholipids and defend against ferroptosis. However, we found that GSH robustly protects a variety of GPX4 knockout (KO) cells from ferroptosis, thus indicating that there is an alternative pathway for GSH to suppress ferroptosis. By carrying out genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening, we identified that ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) is the key factor mediating the GPX4-independent protective effect of GSH. Mechanistically, FSP1 uses GSH to generate reduced ubiquinone, which scavenges oxidized lipids and suppresses ferroptosis. Inhibition of FSP1 abolishes this GSH-dependent ferroptosis protection both in vitro and in vivo. Distinct from NAD(P)H-mediated ubiquinone reduction, GSH-stimulated generation of reduced ubiquinone via FSP1 is independent of flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD). Together, our work clarifies a new mechanism of GSH-mediated ferroptosis suppression, thus highlighting the potential that targeting GSH metabolism should be beneficial for ferroptosis-related diseases whether or not it is related to GPX4.

items.title: STING reprogramming by estrogen promotes neutrophil extracellular trap formation and sex-biased resistance to ADC therapy.
items.abstract: Sex differences in cancer therapy response remain poorly understood. Using a "phase II-like preclinical trial" across 55 CLDN18.2 + pancreatic cancer patient-derived xenografts, we identify marked female-biased resistance to CLDN18.2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapy despite equivalent antigen expression. Mechanistically, estrogen signals through GPER1 to upregulate TRAF6, redirecting tumor-intrinsic STING signaling from IRF3-mediated interferon production toward nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) activation. This drives CXCL1 secretion, neutrophil recruitment, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. NETs form a charged extracellular network that restricts antibody access to tumor-cell-surface antigens-a mechanism we term functional antigen shielding-reducing ADC cytotoxicity independently of antigen expression. The NET burden also correlated with poorer responses to trastuzumab, cetuximab, and enfortumab vedotin across three clinical cohorts. Pharmacologic NET disruption with sivelestat restored ADC efficacy in female mice. These findings reveal an estrogen-driven resistance mechanism with broad implications for antibody-based cancer therapy.

items.title: Identification of a translatable rabbit model for corneal endothelial dysfunction.

sections.objective: To explore the potential of an adult rabbit descemetorhexis model to recapitulate the damage to the endothelium and Descemet's membrane (DM) seen in humans.
sections.methods: Five corneas of 5 female New Zealand rabbits aged 24-26 months underwent 5-mm descemetorhexis; five unwounded corneas from 5 rabbits served as controls. Animals were followed up for 12-week and post-surgical clinical evaluation was performed using slit-lamp, macro images, and optical coherence tomography (OCT). Histological and immunohistochemical analyses were performed post-sacrifice.
sections.results: Corneal transparency analysed by slit-lamp demonstrated that 2 weeks after descemetorhexis, all adult rabbits displayed grade 3 corneal opacity that was reduced to grade 2-3 and remained at this level until the study endpoint. Corroborating these results, quantitative analysis of macro images showed a significant reduction in corneal transparency during the entire follow-up period, with remarkable effect at 2 weeks (P + /K + -ATPase and Zonula occludens-1. An altered collagen matrix with myofibroblasts in the posterior stroma was also found in the surgical center compared with the other analyzed regions in both groups.
sections.conclusion: Our results indicate that descemetorhexis in adult rabbits could be a translatable corneal endothelial dysfunction (CED) model for studying the safety and efficacy of treatments for CED.

items.title: Persistent foetal vasculature: Developmental mechanisms, contemporary management and evolving therapeutics.
items.abstract: Persistent foetal vasculature (PFV) is a spectrum of congenital malformations arising from incomplete regression of the hyaloid-tunica vasculosa lentis complex. Since Reese's original description of persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous and Goldberg's seminal reinterpretation of PFV as a unified developmental spectrum, our understanding has expanded through advances in genetics, imaging, and vitreoretinal surgery. PFV remains one of the most challenging causes of unilateral childhood visual loss. Although modern microsurgical techniques now deliver consistent anatomical success and globe preservation, functional vision is often limited by primary retinal and optic-nerve maldevelopment. This review traces the evolution of PFV management from its embryological basis to current surgical paradigms, integrating evidence from major series and highlighting practical lessons from contemporary vitreoretinal practice.

items.title: Retinoblastoma management: achieving high standards of care.
items.abstract: The current management of retinoblastoma involves chemotherapy by the intravenous, intra-arterial, intravitreous or intra-aqueous delivery routes. These routes can adequately control solid tumour, subretinal seeds, vitreous seeds or aqueous seeds. Intravenous chemotherapy using vincristine, etoposide and carboplatin is commonly used for retinoblastoma control. According to the International Classification of Retinoblastoma, intravenous chemotherapy provides globe salvage with tumour control in 96% of Group A, 90% of Group B and Group C, 68% of Group D and 32% of Group E eyes. Intra-arterial chemotherapy, using melphalan, topotecan and/or carboplatin with delivery from the femoral artery up to the ophthalmic artery to the eye, is particularly used for unilateral retinoblastoma. This alternative has more localised ocular complications but offers more powerful tumour control. Intravitreal chemotherapy, using melphalan and topotecan, can control vitreous seeding, but most specialists employ high-dose topotecan for control of vitreous seeds and some solid tumours and even subretinal seeds. Intra-aqueous chemotherapy, using melphalan or topotecan and can be effective for aqueous seeding. There is still a role for plaque radiotherapy in non-chemotherapy-responsive tumours and enucleation for massive disease that doesn't fully respond to chemotherapy or demonstrates high-risk disease. The management of retinoblastoma has evolved to the current day with several routes of chemotherapy delivery.

items.title: Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Men with High-risk Localized or Metastatic Prostate Cancer Starting Long-term Hormone Therapy in the STAMPEDE Trial.

sections.objective: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) are a leading cause of noncancer death in men with prostate cancer (PCa). Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) improve oncologic outcomes but may exacerbate cardiovascular risk. The Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2(SCORE2) estimates 10-yr cardiovascular risk, yet its validity in men receiving treatment for PCa is untested. To evaluate the cardiovascular safety of ARPIs and other treatment intensification strategies within the STAMPEDE trial and assess SCORE2 performance.
sections.methods: This post hoc analysis included patients allocated to the abiraterone acetate plus prednisolone (AAP), AAP plus enzalutamide (ENZ), docetaxel (DOC), zoledronic acid (ZA), and radiotherapy (RT) comparisons in STAMPEDE with linked health care records in England. Treatment intensification with AAP, AAP plus ENZ, DOC, ZA, or prostate RT in addition to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT).
sections.results: MACE were identified using prespecified International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, and Office of Population Censuses and Surveys Classification of Interventions and Procedures codes. Flexible parametric competing-risk models estimated cumulative incidence and subdistribution hazard ratios (SDHRs). SCORE2 discrimination and calibration were evaluated. A total of 6292 men were included. The 5-yr cumulative MACE incidence with ARPI intensification was 9% in nonmetastatic (M0) disease and 7% in metastatic (M1) disease, comparable to ADT alone. ARPI intensification was not associated with a statistically significant increase in MACE risk (AAP: M0 SDHR 1.15 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.80-1.67], M1 SDHR 1.36 [95% CI 0.87-2.10]; AAP plus ENZ: M0 SDHR 1.34 [95% CI 0.91-1.98], M1 SDHR 1.28 [95% CI 0.85-1.94]). Cardiovascular disease history was the strongest predictor of MACE. Among 5076 patients eligible for SCORE2 assessment, 4239 had complete baseline data. SCORE2 discrimination was modest (10-yr area under the curve 0.63 for M0 disease and 0.61 for M1 disease), and absolute cardiovascular risk was underestimated. Limitations included underrepresentation of patients with severe cardiovascular comorbidity.
sections.conclusion: No statistically significant increase in MACE was observed with ARPIs, DOC, ZA, or prostate RT compared with ADT alone. SCORE2 underestimated cardiovascular risk, supporting development of PCa-specific cardiovascular risk models.

items.title: Statin use is associated with lower risk of open-angle glaucoma incidence and treatment escalation.

sections.objective: Retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX database to explore the relationship between statin use and glaucoma.
sections.methods: The open-angle glaucoma (OAG) incidence analysis consisted of individuals over 40 years of age with statin use and ophthalmological follow-up within 1 year prior. The OAG treatment analysis consisted of individuals with glaucoma and concurrent statin use. Outcomes included rates of OAG onset, topical ocular hypotensive prescription, incisional glaucoma surgery, minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) and selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT).
sections.results: 210 701 matched patients were included in the OAG incidence analysis and 29 598 in the OAG treatment analysis. At 5 years, statin use was associated with lower risk of OAG incidence (HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.82 to 0.89)), as well as treatment escalation to incisional glaucoma surgery (HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.71)), MIGS (HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.41 to 0.50)) or SLT (HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.44)) and lower rates of topical ocular hypotensive prescription (HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.86 to 0.91)). At 10 years, statin use was associated with lower risk of OAG incidence (HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.87 to 0.93)), escalation to incisional glaucoma surgery (HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.75)), MIGS (HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.59)) or SLT (HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.45 to 0.52)) and lower rates of topical ocular hypotensive prescription (HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.86 to 0.91)).
sections.conclusion: Our results suggest that statin use is associated with lower risk of glaucoma onset and treatment escalation. Prospective trials are needed to further elucidate the relationship between statin usage and glaucoma.

items.title: MiKid-QA: construction and performance evaluation of a paediatric myopia education question-answering model.

sections.objective: The surging prevalence of paediatric myopia has overwhelmed clinical education services. While general-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical information, they often lack the domain-specific precision required for specialised care. This study aimed to develop and evaluate Myopia in Kids Question-Answering (MiKid-QA), a paediatric myopia education question-answering model fine-tuned to support standardised patient education.
sections.methods: We conducted a cross-sectional evaluation study. MiKid-QA was developed by fine-tuning the Qwen2.5-32B model using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) on curated professional datasets (2015-2025), including textbooks and expert consensus. Performance was assessed against DeepSeek and GPT-4 through a multicentre, single-blind expert evaluation of 25 standardised clinical scenarios. A panel of specialists rated responses across five dimensions (correctness, completeness, readability, helpfulness and safety) using a 5-point Likert scale.
sections.results: MiKid-QA demonstrated superior automated performance compared with its base model (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy: 0.1423 vs 0.0967). In expert evaluations, MiKid-QA achieved significantly higher scores for correctness (4.43±0.63) and safety (4.38±0.59) compared with DeepSeek and GPT-4 (all p 0.05), MiKid-QA produced more concise responses and lower reading difficulty than GPT-4 (p<0.001), suggesting a potentially favourable balance between information accuracy and patient accessibility in standardised educational scenarios.
sections.conclusion: Specialised fine-tuning on curated myopia-related datasets was associated with higher expert-rated correctness and safety in standardised myopia education scenarios. MiKid-QA may serve as an auxiliary educational tool to support patient communication in myopia care, although further external validation and prospective clinical studies are required before clinical deployment.

items.title: Clinical Messages for Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair from the GLOBALSTAR Registry: Outcomes in Salvage Fenestrated Endovascular Aneurysm Repair, Women, and Octogenarians.

sections.objective: Global Collaborators on Advanced Stent Graft Techniques for Aneurysm Repair (GLOBALSTAR) is a UK registry of complex endovascular aneurysm repair. This study aimed to examine differential outcomes after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) for the following clinically relevant subgroups: women, octogenarians, and salvage FEVAR procedures to rescue previous failed repairs.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective cohort study of GLOBALSTAR. Standard comparative statistics were applied to peri-operative complications; Kaplan-Meier to survival; and cumulative incidence with competing risks to re-intervention and endoleaks. Log rank and Fine-Gray regression tests compared subgroup time to event functions.
sections.results: Over follow up of 1 651 FEVARs, salvage FEVARs experienced a significantly higher risk of re-intervention (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 1.79, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.37 - 2.34; p < .001) and graft related endoleaks type 1a or 1b (sHR 2.37, 95% CI 1.45 - 3.88; p = .001) and type 3 (sHR 2.12, 95% CI 1.36 - 3.32; p = .001) than primary FEVAR. There were more secondary ruptures following salvage FEVAR (4.0% vs. 1.7%; p = .073). Women experienced double the incidence of major complication Clavien-Dindo grades 3 - 5 (22.0% vs. 11.9%; p < .001), threefold incidence of major adverse cardiovascular event (5.9% vs. 2.1%; p = .004), and peri-operative death (5.9% vs. 2.1%; p = .006) compared with men. Median survival was 5.7 years (95% CI, 5.1 - 6.3) for 80 - 84 year olds and 4.8 years (95% CI 4.2 - 6.1) for ≥ 85 year olds. At one year, the overall log rank test showed no significant difference across age strata (p = .11), although octogenarians had worse one year survival than patients aged 65 - 72 years (p = .030).
sections.conclusion: This study generated the following hypotheses: higher rates of re-intervention and graft related endoleak for salvage FEVAR may justify a FEVAR first strategy in appropriate cases, to achieve durable repair. Significantly worse peri-operative outcomes for women require further evaluation and may require changes in pre-operative pathways and case selection. Advanced age alone may not be a strong contraindication to FEVAR and effective case selection may yield acceptable outcomes for octogenarians. This study is limited by its retrospective design but is valuable in terms of its large real world cohort with extended follow up. The results highlight the need for dedicated prospective studies for the three subgroups, to elucidate mechanistic determinants.

items.title: One-year Outcomes of Mechanical Thrombectomy and Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Acute Pulmonary Embolism.

sections.objective: While anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism, mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to compare the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed for up to one year or until death.
sections.results: A total of 724 patients were included: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of cases. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index (sPESI) > 0 (73% vs. 60%, p < 0.001). Age, rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between groups. Median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, IQR 46-89) than CDT (58 minutes, IQR 40-77; p = 0.003). Median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs. 0%, p = 0.048), while CDT was associated with higher ICU admission rates (83% vs. 36%, p < 0.001). However, thirty-day mortality was similar between groups (CDT: 2.6% vs. MT: 4.6%; p = 0.27). Additionally, the one-year incidences of CTEPH (MT: 4.5% vs. CDT: 3.4%, p=0.69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%, p=0.31) and all-cause mortality (MT:7.8% vs. CDT: 5.8%, p=0.41) were not statistically significant between MT and CDT respectfully.
sections.conclusion: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable mortality, CTEPH, and PE recurrence rates at one-year. MT was associated with higher intraoperative cardiac complications, whereas CDT required more frequent ICU admission.

items.title: Efficacy of Cryotherapy in Preventing Taxane-Induced Neuropathy: The CryoPac Randomised Controlled Trial.

sections.objective: Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy (CIPN) is a common and debilitating adverse effect of taxane chemotherapy. Currently there is no established strategy for prevention or treatment. Smaller studies have suggested that cryotherapy may prevent CIPN.
sections.methods: We conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing usual care with cryotherapy using frozen gloves and socks during each taxane treatment. Participants were stratified by site and chemotherapy regiment and randomized 1:1 to cryotherapy or usual care. Eligible patients had a performance status of 0-1. Exclusion criteria included previous taxane chemotherapy, symptoms of CIPN, and a baseline Total Neuropathy Score (TNS) > 0. The primary endpoint was CIPN incidence at the End of Treatment (EoT) defined as TNS ≥2. Secondary endpoints included peripheral neuropathy evaluated with NCI-CTCAE v5.0, patient-reported outcomes using EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 and QLQ-C30, and quantitative sensory testing (QST).
sections.results: A total of 268 patients were randomised; 51 dropped out, leaving 217 for analysis (cryotherapy 123, usual care 94 patients). CIPN incidence at EoT was 78% overall and did not differ significantly between the groups (cryotherapy: 91/123 [74%], 95% CI 0.65 to 0.81; control: 79/94 [84%], 95% CI 0.75 to 0.90; P= .071). Analysis of EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 subscales showed that the cryotherapy group had reduced tingling in hands (P=.025), numbness in hands (P=.025) and feet (p=0.0005), and less trouble manipulating small objects (P=.006). No difference was found in CTCAE grade ≥ 2 CIPN between groups (P = .2). QST showed that cryotherapy reduced tactile disturbance on the monofilament test (P=.006). No difference was observed in QLQ-C30 scores. Cryotherapy did not influence dose modifications. Compliance with cryotherapy was 67%.
sections.conclusion: Cryotherapy did not significantly reduce CIPN incidence (TNS ≥2) at EoT, but cryotherapy treated patients reported fewer sensory symptoms and demonstrated reduced tactile disturbance. Longer follow-up may reveal benefits of cryotherapy for persistent CIPN, supporting possible clinical relevance.

items.title: First-line durvalumab and tremelimumab in poor-prognosis unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: Phase IIIb single-arm SIERRA study.

sections.objective: Clinical trials in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) often exclude patients with poor prognostic factors, including impaired liver function, poor functional status or main trunk portal vein thrombosis (Vp4). The dual immune checkpoint inhibitor regimen STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) is a standard-of-care treatment for first-line uHCC. The phase IIIb SIERRA (NCT05883644) study previously reported early safety of STRIDE in participants of poor prognosis. Here, we present safety and efficacy results from the primary analysis of the SIERRA study. Participants with poor prognosis (e.g. Child-Pugh B/C, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status >1 or main trunk portal vein thrombosis [Vp4]) remain underrepresented in global, phase III trials despite comprising up to 65% of patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) in clinical practice. To address this unmet need, the phase IIIb SIERRA study (NCT05883644) evaluated STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) in participants with poor prognostic factors. Safety and efficacy findings as per the co-primary endpoints are indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need, with an incidence of Grade 3 or 4 PRAEs within 6 months of 19.8% and ORR of 14.4% in the total population. This is the first prospective interventional study to provide data informing the safety and efficacy of STRIDE in patients with uHCC in a previously underrepresented population of poor prognosis that are excluded from other phase III trials. Clinical trial number NCT05883644.
sections.methods: Adults with uHCC with either Child-Pugh B7/B8 liver function (Child-Pugh B7/B8 cohort), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 2 (ECOG PS 2 cohort) or Vp4 (Vp4 cohort) were enrolled. All participants received STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg plus durvalumab 1500 mg once, followed by durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary endpoints were Grade 3 or 4 adverse events possibly related to study treatment within 6 months of treatment initiation (Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months) and objective response rate (ORR; data cut-off: 22 September 2025).
sections.results: In total, 111 participants were included (Child-Pugh B7/B8 n = 44, ECOG PS 2 n = 47, Vp4 n = 20). The incidence of Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 19.8% (12.9-28.5): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 18.2% (8.2-32.7); ECOG PS 2, 19.1% (9.1-33.3); and Vp4, 25.0% (8.7-49.1). ORR (95% CI) was 14.4% (8.5-22.4): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 6.8% (1.4-18.7); ECOG PS 2, 21.3% (10.7-35.7); and Vp4, 15.0% (3.2-37.9).
sections.conclusion: SIERRA safety and efficacy findings were indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need.

items.title: Lipid Burden and Efficacy of Preventive PCI of Vulnerable Atherosclerotic Coronary Plaques: Post Hoc Analysis From the PREVENT Trial.

sections.objective: Preventive percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of non-flow-limiting lesions (fractional flow reserve >0.80) that are high-risk plaques has emerged as a potential strategy to reduce cardiac events. However, identifying which lesions derive the greatest benefit from preventive PCI compared with optimal medical therapy alone remains challenging. This post hoc analysis evaluates the role of the near-infrared spectroscopy-derived lipid core burden index in identifying high-risk plaques that may benefit from preventive PCI.
sections.methods: Among the 1606 patients enrolled in the PREVENT trial (Preventive Coronary Intervention on Stenosis with Functionally Insignificant Vulnerable Plaque) from September 2015 to September 2021, an investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, this post hoc analysis included 598 patients (mean age, 64.1±8.8 years; 27.9% women) comprising 632 lesions with a plaque burden >70% and a minimal lumen area 2 by intravascular ultrasound in whom near-infrared spectroscopy evaluation was also performed. Lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was prespecified as having a maximum lipid core burden index over a 4-mm segment >315. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable or progressive angina.
sections.results: LRPs were present in 223 patients (37.3%) with 234 lesions. During median follow-up of 5.6 years, primary outcome events occurred more frequently in patients with LRPs than in those with non-LRPs (12.5% versus 4.7%; unadjusted hazard ratio, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.03-4.19; P =0.039) in the overall population. Within the LRP group, preventive PCI was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome compared with optimal medical therapy alone (7.3% vs. 17.6%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.13-0.41; P P =0.97). A significant interaction was found between treatment strategy and the presence of LRP ( P interaction <0.001).
sections.conclusion: In this post hoc analysis of the PREVENT trial, preventive PCI was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome in patients with near-infrared spectroscopy-defined LRPs, whereas no significant association was observed in those with non-LRPs despite their large plaque burden and small minimal lumen area. These findings suggest the importance of plaque composition, beyond morphological severity alone, in guiding preventive PCI.

items.title: Incidence, Process of Care, and Outcomes of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in China: A Multicenter Prospective Registry Study.

sections.objective: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is an acute event associated with high mortality. Although survival has improved in high-income countries, contemporary multicenter data from low- and middle-income countries remain scarce, limiting global benchmarking and the identification of system-level opportunities for improvement.
sections.methods: This cohort study used data from the BASIC-IHCA (Baseline Investigation of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest) registry. Adult patients (≥18 years) who experienced IHCA and received cardiopulmonary resuscitation between July 1, 2019, and December 31, 2020, at 37 hospitals across 29 provinces in China were included. The primary outcome was survival to 30 days or hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation, 6- and 12-month survival, and favorable neurological outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score 1-2). Process measures focused on the timeliness of resuscitation response and the implementation of postresuscitation interventions.
sections.results: Among 17 602 patients (median age, 66 years; 65.5% male), the annual incidence of adult IHCA was 4.1 per 1000 admissions. Cardiac etiology was identified in 6569 (37.3%) patients, and 2380 (13.5%) presented with initial shockable rhythm. Among all patients, 16 872 (95.9%) received cardiopulmonary resuscitation within 1 minute; timely defibrillation or epinephrine was achieved in 71.4% and 84.4% of patients with initial shockable and nonshockable rhythms, respectively. Sustained return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 6200 (35.2%) patients, of whom 222 (3.6%) received temperature control therapy and 320 (5.2%) underwent coronary angiography. Overall, 1610 (9.1%) patients survived to 30 days or discharge, with 1241 (7.1%) having a favorable neurological outcome. At 12 months, 1075 (6.1%) patients remained alive, and 986 (5.6%) had a favorable neurological outcome.
sections.conclusion: This multicenter registry highlights a substantial burden of IHCA in China, with markedly low survival rates. Despite prompt initial resuscitation, critical gaps persist in postresuscitation care. Systemic and cultural factors, including the infrequent use of do not attempt cardiopulmonary resuscitation orders, may further contribute to survival disparities. These findings suggest several system-level opportunities to improve IHCA outcomes, including structured response systems, optimized critical care resource allocation, and greater integration of advanced care planning.

items.title: The Oxidized Phospholipid PGPC Impairs Angiogenesis by Inhibiting Endothelial Autophagosomal-Lysosomal Fusion Through NPC1-Induced Syntaxin 17 Acetylation and Ubiquitination.

sections.objective: Angiogenesis is essential for the recovery of ischemic hearts with coronary artery disease (CAD). PGPC (1-palmitoyl-2-glutamyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) is a major phospholipid oxidation product in atherosclerotic lesions. Autophagy participates in angiogenesis. However, whether PGPC affects angiogenesis in ischemic hearts by regulating autophagy remains unclear.
sections.methods: Plasma PGPC concentrations were quantified and the effects of PGPC on angiogenesis were evaluated in cultured endothelial cells and in vivo using a subcutaneous Matrigel plug assay, as well as in hindlimb ischemia and myocardial infarction models in C57BL/6J mice. Autophagic flux and the expression and modification of proteins associated with autophagy and angiogenesis were also assessed.
sections.results: Plasma PGPC levels were increased in patients with CAD, and they were positively correlated with the severity of CAD and negatively correlated with coronary collateral artery formation. PGPC inhibited endothelial cell migration and tube formation. PGPC suppressed neovascularization in Matrigel plugs and reduced blood flow recovery in hindlimb ischemia. In a mouse model of myocardial infarction, PGPC attenuated angiogenesis in the ischemic myocardium. These proangiogenic effects induced by VEGFA (vascular endothelial growth factor A) in ischemic hearts were significantly inhibited by PGPC. Mechanistically, PGPC inhibited the expression of STX17 (syntaxin 17), a crucial molecule that controls autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion by promoting the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitination and degradation of STX17. PGPC upregulated the expression of NPC1 (NPC intracellular cholesterol transporter 1) through CD36 (cluster of differentiation 36). NPC1 not only promoted the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitination and degradation of STX17 through the recruitment of ACAT1 (acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase 1), but also competed with STX17 to bind VAMP8 (vesicle-associated membrane protein 8), leading to inhibition of the expression of eNOS (endothelial nitric oxide synthase), ERK1/2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2), and nitric oxide production. Oxidized phospholipid-neutralizing antibody E06, STX17 overexpression, or silencing of NPC1 reversed the inhibitory effect of PGPC on angiogenesis by restoring autophagic flux.
sections.conclusion: PGPC promotes the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitin-mediated degradation of STX17 by increasing NPC1, leading to a reduction in the level of STX17 associated with VAMP8, which inhibits autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion and angiogenesis. Targeting PGPC, NPC1, or STX17 may represent novel therapeutic approaches to promote angiogenesis in patients with CAD.

items.title: Restenosis after Carotid Artery Stenting in Radiation-induced versus Atherosclerotic Carotid Stenosis: 25-year experience from a tertiary hospital.

sections.objective: To compare the long-term in-stent restenosis (ISR) rate following carotid artery stenting (CAS) in patients with carotid stenosis secondary to atherosclerosis (AS) and radiation-induced stenosis (RIS).
sections.methods: A retrospective review was conducted on 140 CAS procedures in 126 patients at our institution over a 25-year period. Patients with prior neck irradiation were classified as RIS, while the remaining were categorized as AS. Propensity score matching was employed to balance baseline characteristics between the groups. Restenosis was evaluated using specific duplex ultrasound velocity criteria validated for stented arteries. Rates of moderate (≥50%) and severe (≥70%) in-stent restenosis were compared, and long-term restenosis-free survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Multivariate logistic regression was used to determine independent risk factors for ISR.
sections.results: After matching, 40 CAS procedures were included in each group (RIS and AS). Median follow-up duration was 72 months. The RIS group exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of ≥50% ISR (40% vs. 12.5%; p=0.005) and a composite endpoint of ≥50% ISR or new stenosis outside the stented segment (55% vs. 17.5%; p<0.001). The estimated 2-year ISR-free survival at ≥50% was 75.5% in RIS compared to 94.8% in AS (p=0.005). Multivariate analysis identified prior neck irradiation as the sole independent risk factor for ≥50% ISR (OR 7.05, 95% CI 1.26-39.45, p=0.026). No significant risk factors were found for ≥70% ISR. Era-based analysis demonstrated a significant decrease in the incidence of ≥50% and ≥70% ISR in the RIS group during the more recent period, accompanied by shifts in baseline characteristics such as prevalence of hyperlipidema and statin use. Reintervention rate and late ipsilateral neurological events were comparable between the groups.
sections.conclusion: Radiation-induced carotid stenosis is associated with higher rates of long-term moderate (≥50%) in-stent restenosis following carotid artery stenting compared with atherosclerotic disease. However, reintervention and late ipsilateral neurological event rates remain comparable between groups. Recent temporal declines in restenosis coincide with increased statin use and optimized hyperlipidemia management.

items.title: Development and Internal Validation of the Si-AAA Prognostic Score for Five-Year Overall Survival after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in Patients with Asymptomatic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.

sections.objective: Although endovascular aneurysm repair is widely used for the treatment of asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm, long-term survival is influenced by patient comorbidities and aneurysm-related characteristics. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair.
sections.methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair. Candidate predictors included demographic, clinical, aneurysm-related, and laboratory variables. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of 5-year mortality. Continuous predictors were categorized using clinically interpretable thresholds derived from time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and a simplified point-based score was constructed from regression coefficients. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's concordance index, and internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples to obtain an optimism-corrected concordance index. Calibration was evaluated using bootstrap-based calibration plots.
sections.results: A total of 445 patients were screened, and 443 complete cases were included in the final analysis. During follow-up, 133 deaths (30.0%) occurred. The estimated 5-year overall survival rate was 62.8% (95% CI, 57.8%-68.0%). Independent predictors of 5-year mortality included age >70 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.66, 95% CI 1.06-2.62; P = .029), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.08-2.69; P = .023), unfit status (aHR 2.32, 95% CI 1.58-3.39; P < .001), serum albumin ≤3.5 g/dL (aHR 2.80, 95% CI 1.97-3.98; P < .001), and abdominal aortic aneurysm diameter ≥7 cm (aHR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.38; P = .023). The final score ranged from 0 to 7. The apparent concordance index was 0.721, with an optimism-corrected concordance index of 0.713 after bootstrap validation. Risk stratification showed clear separation between low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (5-year overall survival: 82.5%, 53.4%, and 23.8%, respectively; log-rank P < .001).
sections.conclusion: A simple prognostic scoring system incorporating age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unfit status, serum albumin, and aneurysm diameter demonstrated acceptable discrimination and good calibration for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. This tool may assist in risk stratification and long-term clinical decision-making. As this score was derived and internally validated in a single-center cohort, external validation in independent cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

items.title: Association of Race and Socioeconomic Status with Hemodialysis Arteriovenous Access Outcomes.

sections.objective: Arteriovenous access is essential for long-term hemodialysis. The creation and maintenance of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) or arteriovenous graft (AVG) are critical for effective dialysis and minimizing complications. However, the influence of race and social determinants of health on presentation, management, and outcomes has not been well evaluated. This study uses the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database to evaluate disparities in vascular access outcomes by race and community-level disadvantage.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective study using the VQI database to identify adults who underwent AVF or AVG creation for hemodialysis between 2016 and 2023. The Area Deprivation Index (ADI), a validated measure of neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage incorporating income, education, employment, and housing quality, was categorized into quartiles from least (Q1) to most disadvantaged (Q4). Patients without follow-up data, recorded complications, or ADI information were excluded. Predisposing factors and postoperative outcomes considering race and ADI were analyzed.
